title: GeoLock Artifact Composer for Automated SOC2/ISO Evidence
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a composer service (GeoLock Artifact Composer) that automatically assembles, validates, signs, and surfaces bundled compliance artifacts demonstrating data residency and retention controls for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits. The composer should consume evidence emitted by collectors across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, normalize metadata (region, retention policy, control mapping), create immutable bundles with cryptographic proofs, and provide an auditor-facing export and API for evidence queries.
context: Current Collector workstreams produce scattered artifacts (logs, config snapshots, policy assertions, S3 retention tags, audit events). Auditors require concise, traceable bundles that map artifacts to control statements (e.g., CC6.1 / A.8.2) and assert residency + retention windows. Manual collation is time-consuming and error-prone; customers with regional compliance needs are requesting automated packaged attestations. This initiative closes the gap between raw telemetry and auditor-grade evidence packages.
solution_outline: 1) Define a standard Evidence Manifest schema (JSON) that includes control mapping, jurisdiction tags, retention assertions, timestamps, producer signature, and content digests. 2) Implement Composer service that: - ingests manifests from collectors, - validates schema and artifact availability, - normalizes region/retention semantics, - packages artifacts into versioned bundles with a manifest and signed hash chain, - stores bundles in a tamper-evident retention vault (S3 + object lock or on-prem equivalent), - exposes REST API + signed downloadable bundle. 3) Integrate KMS signing and timestamping (HSM/KMS) and provide an audit UI in Console to inspect bundles and run simple pre-audit checks.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence Manifest schema published and reviewed by Security & GRC
Composer can ingest sample manifests from three collector types (platform logs, config snapshot, retention tags) and produce a signed bundle
Bundles include mapping to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 control IDs based on the mapping table
Bundles are stored with immutability metadata and retrievable via API and Console within expected SLO (95th percentile < 2s for metadata lookup)
Automated pre-audit validation runs (schema + artifact availability + signature verification) return pass/fail with actionable errors
Integration tests cover injection of incorrect manifests and ensure Composer surfaces clear remediation steps
Documentation and an auditor export template available in Confluence
Security review sign-off and KMS/HSM proof-of-concept completed
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misclassification of region or retention could invalidate an audit. Mitigation: strict normalization rules and confidence metadata; require source collectors to include authoritative region tags and fallback to cloud provider region when missing.

Risk: Large artifact bundles increase storage/costs. Mitigation: support delta manifests and references (not duplicating large objects), plus tiered retention indices and sample-based attestations for high-volume telemetry.
Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: HSM-backed keys, rotate per-release, and bundle-level revocation/rotation metadata.

Risk: Private deployments with air-gapped constraints cannot call KMS. Mitigation: provide an offline signing shim and instructions for customer-side signing or transfer of signing artifacts under secure channels.
Risk: Compliance mapping drift as controls evolve. Mitigation: maintain a mapping registry with change logs and automated impact notifications to downstream bundles.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Schema design, security review, POC for bundle signing. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Composer ingestion pipeline, validation layer, basic bundle storage. Phase 3 (3 weeks): KMS/HSM integration, Console view, API endpoints, and exporter. Phase 4 (2 weeks): QA, integration with collectors, runbook for auditors, documentation and release.
milestones: Composer beta with ingest and storage (2026-03-29)
notes: Prefer a small, extensible manifest that can reference large objects by digest/URL instead of embedding. Align control mapping with SOC 2 CC / ISO 27001 Annex A IDs and include human-readable rationale for each mapped artifact. Coordinate with Legal on retention disclosure language. Expect follow-up work for policy-driven auto-remediation attachments.
